articles.title: Nvidia chip scandal: How Alice Huang's $270 million network is linked to China's military
articles.summary: New records reviewed by Reuters shed light on the sprawling business network around Alice Huang, whose family and associates financed hundreds of millions
articles.body: New records reviewed by Reuters shed light on the sprawling business network around Alice Huang, whose family and associates financed hundreds of millions of dollars in AI computing equipment in China. With many of the links within the network connecting to China’s military.Companies linked to Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman at the centre of the Nvidia chip scandal, used artificial intelligence servers and computing modules worth $270 million to secure financing in China.The records, filed in a Chinese central-bank credit registry, identify up to 764 AI servers and computing modules, along with $31 million in networking equipment used to connect large computing systems. Much of the hardware was listed at a sprawling Shanghai data centre developed by gaming company Century Huatong, in which Chinese technology giant Tencent holds a minority stake.The financing arrangements offer a fresh look at how businesses connected to Huang’s family and associates helped build and fund China’s AI computing infrastructure, even as US authorities investigate whether her Singapore-based company Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain restricted Nvidia technology.The network has also drawn scrutiny over its links to China’s defence sector and the People’s Liberation Army (PLA). Corporate records and research by intelligence firm Strider Technologies, reviewed by The New York Times, have connected companies associated with Huang’s family and business partners to Chinese state-owned defence contractors and military-linked businesses.The connections do not establish that the servers identified in the latest Reuters report were used by the PLA or contained chips prohibited from export to China.Hundreds of servers backed financingOne of the key businesses involved was Century Litong, an Nvidia preferred cloud partner that rents powerful servers to customers requiring large amounts of computing capacity.Financial records show five leasing arrangements covering up to 512 servers, with a declared value of 1.42 billion yuan, or about $200 million, between May and December 2024.Four of the arrangements listed equipment at the Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing centre in Shanghai, a complex developed by Century Huatong. Tencent holds roughly 10% of Century Huatong.A separate transaction involved 128 servers worth $57 million, financed by an arm of the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), a state-backed aviation and defence conglomerate, and leased to Century Litong.Another inventory listed more than 10,000 Nvidia ConnectX-7 networking cards and 730 BlueField-3 units at the Shanghai facility. The equipment is used to connect large numbers of computers for AI workloads.In April 2026, Wuhu Century Longteng, a company majority-owned by Huang’s sister Huang Yu through investment vehicles until early 2026, pledged another 252 AI computing modules as collateral for a $70 million loan from Ping An Bank.The dollar values reflect assets covered by financing arrangements and do not necessarily represent new spending or separate purchases.How the network connects to China’s defence industryThe latest records add to questions about the business network surrounding Alice Huang, her sister Huang Yu and Kang Wei, her business partner, who is often described as her husband.Corporate records connect Century Litong, Century Longteng and Century Huatong to Huang Yu and Kang. Century Litong was established in 2023 as a subsidiary of Shanghai Century Longteng and later came under the ownership of Jiangsu Lettall Electronic.Lettall also owns Nanjing Jinning Microwave, a manufacturer of components used in Chinese radar and missile systems, according to company disclosures and research cited by The New York Times.The network also has links to AVIC, the state-owned aerospace and defence conglomerate, through financing arrangements involving its affiliate. Other corporate connections identified by Strider include China Electronics Technology Group, a military-electronics conglomerate.A Strider analysis reviewed by The New York Times found that about $3.6 billion in Chinese government money had flowed through companies associated with Huang’s family and business associates.“Follow the money and, too often, you find the PLA at the end of it,” Strider chief executive Greg Levesque told the newspaper.The links are often indirect. The research does not establish that the PLA used computing power from data centres connected to Huang’s family.Tencent’s presence and the limits of the linkTencent’s minority stake in Century Huatong has brought another prominent Chinese technology company into the scrutiny surrounding the network.The US Department of Defense included Tencent on its list of Chinese military companies operating in the United States under Section 1260H. The designation identifies companies the Pentagon considers linked to China’s military; it does not itself impose an immediate ban.Tencent has disputed the designation, saying it was a mistake and that the company was not a military supplier.The company also told Reuters that it had never owned or operated the Yangtze River Delta Data Center Cluster Project and that its name and trademarks had previously been used without authorisation. Tencent said its investment in Century Huatong was related to the gaming business and that it had no commercial relationship with Megaspeed.The records reviewed by Reuters do not establish that Tencent bought, rented or operated the specific servers identified in the financing documents.Megaspeed under US scrutinyAlice Huang formerly controlled Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company and major overseas buyer of Nvidia processors. The US Commerce Department added the company to its trade blacklist on Monday.Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Huang left the company in August 2025.Separately, US intelligence agencies have reportedly gathered information about Huang’s contacts with China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), including during part of her relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The agencies are also said to have gathered evidence suggesting Kang Wei worked with the same intelligence agency, according to reports citing people familiar with the intelligence.The extent of the alleged intelligence work remains under investigation. China has denied allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.The latest financing records do not establish that the servers contained export-restricted chips or show how and when the equipment entered China. They do, however, reveal the scale of the computing infrastructure financed by companies connected to Huang’s family and associates, a network which also finds its ties to the Chinese military.You use AI every day. articles.title: Halifax couple Paul and Jane Bottomley have raised £86,000 for a hospital cancer centre through Christmas hamper raffles that Paul started to give back to Calderdale Royal Hospital after Jane began chemotherapy
articles.summary: A Christmas fundraising tradition that began as a way to support a hospital treating his wife has become a major source of help for cancer patients.
articles.body: A Christmas fundraising tradition that began as a way to support a hospital treating his wife has become a major source of help for cancer patients. Paul and Jane Bottomley, from Sowerby Bridge near Halifax, have raised £86,000 for the Macmillan Cancer Information Centre at Calderdale Royal Hospital through annual Christmas hamper raffles.The idea came about when Jane was diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2012 and began chemotherapy at the hospital. Paul wanted to contribute towards the place where his wife was receiving treatment. He started collecting donations for Christmas hampers and selling raffle tickets to raise money for the cancer unit. The BBC reported the couple's latest fundraising total and Paul's recent cancer diagnosis.Over the years, the annual initiative has grown into a regular Christmas event. The couple collect food, drinks, gifts and other items, pack them into hampers and sell tickets for a chance to win them. The proceeds go towards facilities and resources for people undergoing cancer treatment.Jane received the all-clear in 2023, but the couple's experience with cancer has not ended there. Paul, 59, has now been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is due to have his prostate removed in December. After years of helping other patients, he is preparing to receive treatment himself.Fundraising that started during wife's treatmentJane's ovarian cancer diagnosis led to the beginning of the couple's fundraising work. While she was undergoing chemotherapy at Calderdale Royal Hospital, Paul decided to organise a Christmas raffle to support the hospital's Macmillan unit.The campaign continued in the following years, with donations from individuals and businesses helping the couple put together the hampers. The money has supported several improvements at the cancer centre, benefiting patients and their families.The funds have helped pay for a coffee machine, televisions, books for children whose parents have cancer and cold caps used to reduce hair loss during chemotherapy. These purchases have added to the facilities available to patients visiting the centre.The Halifax Courier, in its December 2025 report, documented how the fundraising had crossed £80,000 after 11 years. It also reported that the money had helped the unit purchase wheelchairs, machines, trolleys, cutlery, books and DVDs.Paul's cancer diagnosis changes this year's campaignThe latest fundraising drive has become particularly personal for Paul. He had spent years helping people affected by cancer, including members of his own family, but had not expected to face the disease himself.Paul initially thought his frequent need to urinate at night was an effect of getting older. He later learnt that he had prostate cancer and would need surgery.Cancer has affected several members of his family. His mother was diagnosed with liver cancer when he was 17. His father developed throat cancer when he was 26. His sister Maria died five years ago, with stomach cancer suspected as the cause. His brother also died from cancer a year ago.Describing the repeated losses, Paul said to BBC: "It's just one thing after another." His diagnosis has also been difficult for Jane, who had completed her own treatment and received the all-clear. She found it hard to process the news that her husband was now facing cancer. "I just felt empty, really. I thought is this real?" she said.Jane also spoke about the emotional impact of seeing her husband go through a similar experience after her own recovery. "I've got rid of mine and now it's his turn. I felt blank, I couldn't take it in," she said.Paul said waiting for his operation had been particularly difficult. "I can't think, I can't rest, it's just a waiting game. I have my operation in December," he said.Six Christmas hampers prepared for raffleDespite his diagnosis, Paul has continued organising the annual fundraising campaign. Their spare room is currently being used to store donations collected for this year's draw. These include food, drinks, snacks, toiletries and games.The couple will put together six Super Hampers, each valued at more than £400. Raffle tickets are being sold for £1, giving participants a chance to win one of the hampers. The winners will be announced through a social media draw in the week before Christmas.The campaign has received regular support over the years, with people looking forward to the annual raffle. Paul said the response had remained encouraging, even as his own circumstances had changed."Everyone looks forward to the hampers, and this year it's special because this time I need to take something back from the Macmillan unit," he said.For Paul, continuing the work has also provided something to concentrate on while he waits for treatment. "Sorting the hampers is the only thing that's kept me going. To be honest with you, I never thought it would happen to me," he said.He admitted that receiving the diagnosis had been difficult to accept, particularly after spending so much time raising money for people with cancer. "I struggled with the diagnosis after all the money I raised, thinking, 'why me?'" he said.Cancer centre pledges support to the coupleThe Macmillan Cancer Information and Support Service in Halifax has seen the benefits of the couple's fundraising over the years. Its facilities include resources intended to make the experience of patients and their families more comfortable.Amanda Davies, who works at the centre, praised Paul and Jane for turning their own difficult experiences into support for other people facing cancer."The way Paul and Jane have come through adversity to make it better for other people going through similar experiences - it's heartwarming," she said.She also acknowledged Paul's contribution to the centre and said its staff would stand by him as he prepares for treatment. "Paul is a genuine kind soul who's made a huge difference," Davies said. "We will be here to carry on supporting him and help him navigate the future."Paul said he had never imagined that he would become a cancer patient after years of supporting others. His experience has reinforced his belief that the disease can affect anyone. "It doesn't discriminate - it doesn't matter who you are, you're just never safe. You've got to live your life," he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Himachal consumer court orders Decathlon to refund Rs 10,067 with 9% interest, says refund receipt failed to prove money reached customer's account; also awards Rs 10,000 for harassment, costs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer court in Himachal Pradesh as directed Decathlon Sports India to refund Rs 10,067 to a Dharamshala man after finding that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer court in Himachal Pradesh as directed Decathlon Sports India to refund Rs 10,067 to a Dharamshala man after finding that the company failed to prove that the amount paid for cancelled hiking shoes was credited to his bank account. The commission also ordered it to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.Why did the Decathlon customer seek a refund?The complainant, Akshay Thakur, had placed an online order through Decathlon's shopping application on October 10, 2025, for two pairs of men's mid-ankle hiking shoes priced at Rs 4,999 each. After adding delivery charges of Rs 69, he paid Rs 10,067 through UPI.He alleged that he realised immediately after placing the order that he had selected the wrong size and quantity and attempted to cancel it. However, the application generated another order for the same product, size and quantity. He subsequently cancelled the replacement order, selecting "ordered by mistake" as the reason.Although the company promised a refund within seven to 10 working days, the complainant alleged that the amount was never credited despite repeated reminders and calls to customer support.Decathlon contested the complaint, claiming that the full Rs 10,067 had been refunded to his source account on October 10, 2025. It produced a refund processing receipt and alleged that Thakur had filed a false complaint despite receiving his money.What did the commission say?The bench comprising president Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur noted that Decathlon had failed to produce a bank statement, clearing house confirmation or any other financial record proving that the refund was actually credited.The commission said merely showing an internal processing status or refund timeline was insufficient to establish that the customer had received the money."The failure of the Opposite Party to place any concrete proof of actual credit on record leaves the claim of the complainant unrebutted on this material aspect," the commission observed.It also disapproved of the company's allegations that Thakur, an advocate, had filed the complaint to obtain unjust monetary gains, observing that he had merely exercised his statutory consumer right.The commission held that withholding the money, coupled with inadequate communication and customer support, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.Final orderPronounced on November 13, 2026, the commission directed Decathlon Sports India to:Refund Rs 10,067 with 9 percent annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until realisation.Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental agony, humiliation and harassment.Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday said NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar could have been considered for the 2022 presidential election by Prime Minister Narendra Modi had he joined the BJP-led NDA in 2019.Athawale told news agency IANS that he had repeatedly persuaded the veteran politician to join the alliance on the basis of a common minimum programme."I was the one who had suggested that Sharad Pawar should join the NDA in 2019. From 2014 to 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi accelerated the country's development, and significant progress was made across several sectors," he said.Athawale said Modi held Pawar in high regard and recalled that the prime minister had considered the NCP (SP) chief his ideal during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister."Prime Minister Narendra Modi believes in development, and our mission is to make India the world's number one economy by 2047. He has always held Sharad Pawar in high regard. When Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat, he used to say that he considered Pawar his ideal. Therefore, I believe Sharad Pawar should have joined the NDA. Had he joined in 2019, perhaps Prime Minister Narendra Modi would have considered him for the 2022 presidential election," the Union minister told IANS.On seat-sharing talks between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Athawale said the two INDIA bloc partners could struggle to reach an agreement and might even contest separately."I do not know what compromise will be reached between the two parties, but I do not think the Samajwadi Party will offer them so many seats. However, the decision rests with them," he said.Commenting on the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) renewing their alliance ahead of Punjab assembly elections, Athawale said the move would strengthen the NDA's prospects in the state.Recalling the alliance's tenure under former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, he said the two parties had remained in power for several years.Athawale also claimed that people in Punjab were increasingly dissatisfied with the Aam Aadmi Party government, citing concerns over drug trafficking, the condition of young people and farmers' issues.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bill Gates and Melinda French got divorced in May 2021, everything about the divorce settlement has been kept secret, except this one 'Microsoft number'
articles.summary: When Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates announced their divorce in May 2021, they kept the financial details of their separation private.
articles.body: When Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates announced their divorce in May 2021, they kept the financial details of their separation private. The former couple did not publicly reveal how their estimated fortune was divided or whether they had signed a prenuptial agreement. However, one major figure emerged from public filings: around $1.8 billion worth of stock transferred to Melinda French Gates from Cascade Investment on May 3, 2021. The investment firm was built using money Bill Gates earned through Microsoft dividends and share sales, making the transfer a notable link between the couple's divorce and the tech billionaire's Microsoft wealth.What was the $1.8 billion stock transferAccording to public filings, Cascade Investment transferred around 14.1 million shares of Canadian National Railway and nearly 3 million shares of AutoNation to Melinda French Gates. At the time, the holdings were valued at approximately $1.5 billion and $309 million, respectively.The transfers did not stop there. On May 13, 2021, Cascade also transferred around $851 million worth of Deere & Co. stock to her. Forbes' review of SEC filings found that publicly disclosed stock transfers to Melinda had crossed $3 billion by then.The timing of the transfers suggests they were connected to the divorce settlement, although the exact terms of the agreement have never been made public.Why did Bill Gates transfer shares instead of cashThere is a financial reason why couples may choose to transfer investments directly during a divorce rather than sell them and divide the money. Under US federal tax law, transfers of property between spouses, or former spouses as part of a divorce, are generally not taxable at the time of transfer.“The biggest reason is taxes,” family mediator and Certified Divorce Financial Analyst Kristyn Carmichael told Moneywise.She explained that selling shares worth $1.8 billion to pay the other spouse in cash could create a large capital gains tax bill for the seller.Why stock worth $100,000 may not mean $100,000 in cashCarmichael also warned that people receiving shares in a divorce should check what the original owner paid for them. “$100,000 in stock is not the same as $100,000 in cash,” she said.For example, if someone receives shares worth $100,000 that their spouse originally bought for $10,000, selling them could mean paying taxes on the $90,000 gain.Michelle Smith, a certified divorce financial analyst, also advised couples to compare investments after accounting for taxes. “If you take lower-basis stock while your spouse keeps cash, you may have taken the smaller half without realizing it,” she told Moneywise.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: An Illinois property owner faced $53,000 in additional fines over scrap vehicles, pallets and other debris on his land; appeals court vacates fines but upholds nuisance finding
articles.summary: An Illinois appeals court has cancelled about $53,000 in daily fines against a Mattoon man, as the city never charged him for the days it sought to
articles.body: An Illinois appeals court has cancelled about $53,000 in daily fines against a Mattoon man, as the city never charged him for the days it sought to penalise him. However, the court upheld the finding that his two properties on Broadway Avenue were a public nuisance, along with the original $750 fine.The Fifth District Appellate Court issued the opinion on Monday, 23 November, closing a case that began in 2018. Tim Quackenbush, who owns the properties, has run a demolition and excavation business since 1978. The city says his land became a dumping ground for scrap metal, wooden pallets, plastic totes, a hot tub and inoperable vehicles. Quackenbush argued that the materials were stock for his business and that the zoning allowed them.Legal complications with the cityThe city filed a complaint in September 2018, describing a day's worth of problems. In January 2020, a trial judge found that the properties were a nuisance and fined him $750. He could get the fine reduced to $100 if he cleaned up. However, he did not, at least not sufficiently. So the case remained open for years, with multiple hearings, two site visits and orders telling him what to fix. But progress remained slow.During a 2021 hearing, Quackenbush was asked if he had completed the cleanup. “Well, it depends on what you call done,” Quackenbush, the defendant, said. He told the court that he had cleaned up certain areas and was allowed to keep “all these items”. He added that he did not know why “the City seems to think that I have to put them in a certain order, or I have to get rid of a certain amount”.Back in 2019, the police chief stated that progress was “close to none”. As the properties remained messy, the judge added $50 a day for 101 days. In a January 2025 final order, the judge added another $50 for each of 959 days. Those additional fines brought the total to $53,750.What the appeals court foundThe majority opinion focused on the wording of the city's rules rather than the state of the properties. The rules allow the city to issue a new ticket for each day a problem continues. However, they also say that fines can only be imposed for tickets the city has already issued. The city issued one ticket, so the court said it could only collect one fine.The court also observed that the additional fines were unfair, as Quackenbush had not been formally charged with those additional violations and had no opportunity to defend himself against them in court. The judges also noted that the trial judge had said the city could make him remove items but had never ordered him to do so. This made the fines appear more like a punishment than a means of cleaning up the property.The court agreed that the properties were a nuisance. Photos from the trial showed open tubs, barrels, a dumpster and piles of pallets. The judges agreed that these conditions were likely to attract insects and rats. The zoning argument did not work either. Land can be zoned for industrial use and still be a nuisance if it is not properly maintained, the court said.While Justice Barberis agreed that the properties were a nuisance, he disagreed with removing the $53,000 in fines. He read the city's general fine rules together with the nuisance rules. He pointed to a 2022 case from another Illinois appeals court that had interpreted similar city rules together. He also said the word “may” in the rules gave the city a choice, rather than an obligation, to issue a new ticket each day.Justice Barberis disagreed that the additional fines were unfair. He said the judge had fined the defendant only for specific periods supported by evidence, not for an unlimited number of days. He also said that six years of court hearings had given Quackenbush sufficient warning that he could face additional fines.The opinion is a draft, which means it may change before the court issues its final decision or considers a request for rehearing. For now, the court has removed the additional $53,000 in fines but retained the original $750 fine and the ruling that the properties were a public nuisance.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP), accusing its leadership of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP), accusing its leadership of practising family-centric politics and failing to respect the sentiments of devotees of Lord Ram.“Radhe Radhe is just the beginning. Time for Ram Naam Satya is approaching for the SP,” Adityanath said, taking a swipe at the party during an interview at the ABP Conclave, as cited by news agency PTI.The chief minister also targeted SP president Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to Ayodhya, saying those who tried to sail in two boats would eventually drown.CM Adityanath said the SP leadership should apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus for the firing on devotees in the 1990s. “If the SP leadership had shown some wisdom in the 1990s, bullets would not have been fired at Ram devotees. They should now apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus,” he said, according to a press statement of the interview.Explaining his remark, CM Yogi said greetings should reflect local religious traditions, with 'Radhe Radhe' appropriate in Mathura, 'Jai Shri Ram' in Ayodhya and 'Har Har Mahadev' in Kashi.He added that 'Ram Naam Satya' was traditionally associated with a person's final journey.CM Yogi calls SP slogan ‘Parivar Development Authority’Taking aim at the SP's PDA slogan, CM Adityanath described it as “Parivar Development Authority”, alleging that the party's politics was limited to the interests of its own family.He also criticised the SP-Congress alliance, claiming it had run into trouble even before the elections because of differences over seat-sharing. The chief minister pointed to the two parties announcing candidates while negotiations were still under way.The seat-sharing discussions have remained inconclusive after two rounds of meetings. The SP announced five candidates on Tuesday, prompting criticism from Congress leaders.Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the SP should have waited until the negotiations were over. “They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over),” he told PTI, while expressing hope that the discussions would proceed in the right direction.Congress MP Imran Masood also questioned the SP's move, saying simultaneous talks and candidate announcements suggested that the party was not serious about the negotiations. He said the Congress would consult its leadership on whether discussions should continue.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, urged the Congress to focus on “winning equations” rather than the number of seats. He asked the party to share a list of constituencies it was interested in contesting beyond the 26 seats proposed by the SP, so that both parties could jointly assess which candidate was best placed to win.Adityanath said the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance allies would contest the elections together, with candidates selected through the party's established process.CM cites economic growth, investment and jobsOn the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, CM Adityanath said the exercise was necessary to remove the names of deceased voters and people who had shifted elsewhere.“Every eligible Indian citizen should have a place on the voter list, but a foreign national cannot have voting rights,” he said, accusing the SP of supporting infiltrators while questioning Indian citizens.The chief minister also highlighted what he described as Uttar Pradesh's economic transformation since 2017, saying the state's economy, per capita income and budget had grown more than threefold. He claimed the state had moved from being a “BIMARU” state to a growth engine.Contrasting the state's industrial landscape with that under previous governments, CM Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had moved from illegal country-made pistol and bomb factories to manufacturing revolvers, rifles and BrahMos missiles.He said the state had received investment proposals worth Rs 50 lakh crore and introduced 36 sector-specific policies to attract investors. Uttar Pradesh, he added, accounted for 55 per cent of India's mobile phone production and 60 per cent of electronic component manufacturing.The chief minister said the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector and the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative were providing employment to 3.25 crore people. He also claimed that housing disputes involving four lakh homebuyers had been resolved through dialogue between builders and buyers.On employment, he said the government had issued nearly 9.75 lakh appointment letters to young people and aimed to increase the number to 10.5 lakh by January 26.Warning those threatening the safety of women, traders and investors, he said people who cast an evil eye on daughters, traders and women moving on the streets would have only two destinations — “jail or jahannum”.CM Yogi described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his role model and said he was an ordinary party worker who would discharge whatever responsibility was assigned to him.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Streamer N3ON's Hawaii vacation has taken an unexpected turn after he and Nevaeh reportedly got into a heated argument with a local man over the price of a Hula dance lesson. articles.title: 'Kyiv in 3 days' to 5th year of war: Leaked Russian records reveal nearly 500,000 killed since start of invasion
articles.summary: In early February 2022, weeks before Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, US intelligence assessments predicted that Kyiv could fall within
articles.body: In early February 2022, weeks before Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, US intelligence assessments predicted that Kyiv could fall within 72 hours of an attack.But the war did not unfold as Moscow had expected. Nearly five years later, what was supposed to be a swift military campaign has turned into a prolonged war of attrition, with largely hardened frontlines.According to a BBC analysis of leaked Russian government records, nearly half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the invasion began in February 2022.The scale of Russia's losses has now emerged from inside its own government system. An investigation by BBC Russian, based on more than 11 million leaked death records from Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat), has identified 490,334 Russian military deaths since the invasion began in February 2022.The findings offer one of the most detailed pictures yet of the human cost of a war whose actual death toll Moscow has kept largely under wraps.The BBC analysed the leaked records in collaboration with independent Russian media outlet Mediazona, cross-checking them against its database of confirmed Russian military deaths.The investigation identified military fatalities through recorded causes of death, employment and military service details, as well as court rulings declaring missing soldiers dead.Of the 490,334 deaths identified, 51,067 were established through court rulings, highlighting the number of soldiers who disappeared on the battlefield and were later legally declared dead.However, the figure of 490,334 may not represent the full scale of Russian military deaths. The BBC said its analysis identified deaths recorded in the leaked database, while independent estimates based on documented fatalities suggest the actual toll could be considerably higher.Military experts estimate that publicly documented deaths account for only 45 to 55 percent of the total, putting the possible Russian military death toll between 527,295 and 644,471.Beyond the death toll, the investigation also reveals how deeply the war has affected Russia's younger male population.In 2025, war-related deaths accounted for 65 percent of all deaths among Russian men aged 18 to 24 and 59 percent among those aged 25 to 34, according to the BBC analysis. The findings point to the growing demographic cost of the invasion, with the conflict claiming a significant share of lives among men in their prime working and military recruitment years.On the battlefield, the war remains concentrated in eastern Ukraine, particularly the Donetsk region, where Russian forces continue to push towards key Ukrainian defensive positions around Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka.Despite sustained assaults, territorial gains have been slow and the roughly 1,250-km frontline has remained largely static in recent months. Ukrainian forces continue to resist Russian advances, while both sides have intensified drone and missile strikes, including attacks on energy infrastructure.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump called Abdul El-Sayed a 'jihadist' during midterms, now he wants to meet him over Trumpcare
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump plans a meeting with Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed to discuss the universal healthcare proposal named 'Trumpcare', signaling a potential shift in bipartisan collaboration in Congress.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said he intends to meet Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed to discuss the Democrat’s proposal for universal healthcare, after unexpectedly endorsing his suggestion to brand the plan as “Trumpcare”.In an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, Trump described El-Sayed as a “smart guy” and praised his decision to associate the president’s name with the healthcare proposal. He also suggested that the two could find common ground despite their political differences.“He’s a smart guy. He did a good job. He actually did a very good job,” Trump told the newspaper during a 45-minute interview at the Oval Office.“I know I’ll be meeting with him. Maybe there’s some place in the middle that we could go,” he added.El-Sayed, who made universal healthcare a central issue during his Senate campaign, proposed renaming his Medicare for All plan “Trumpcare” earlier this month. He shared an image of a gold-coloured healthcare card bearing the name on X and challenged Trump to support a system that would provide healthcare coverage “from cradle to grave”.Trump drew attention to the proposal on Saturday by reposting a screenshot of El-Sayed’s post. During Tuesday’s interview, he described the branding idea as “very smart”, according to the New York Post.The president also indicated that he was open to working with Democrats in Congress, although he predicted that negotiations could begin with disagreements. Democrats are set to control both chambers of Congress during the final two years of Trump’s presidency.“I’m just going to veto everything there is, and then at some point I think they’re going to want to negotiate. I will, and we can do health care. We can do a lot of great things together,” Trump said.The proposed meeting marks a change in tone after months of hostility between the two during the midterm election campaign.Trump repeatedly targeted El-Sayed at rallies, at one point referring to him as “Mohammed” and falsely describing the former public health official as a “jihadist”.Trump had earlier warned that an El-Sayed victory would be “a devastating blow for our country”.The Democrat also frequently criticised Trump and Vice President JD Vance during his campaign. Responding to attacks over his name and faith, El-Sayed said these issues were not responsible for the financial pressures facing ordinary Americans.“They can keep saying my name. They can keep pointing to my faith. My name and my faith are not the reason you can’t afford your groceries,” he said in the closing days of the race.Despite the exchanges, El-Sayed has indicated that he is willing to meet the president if doing so could help advance his legislative priorities. Speaking on ABC’s This Week earlier this month, he said he would be open to discussions with Trump or other political figures, irrespective of party affiliation.“I’ve never met the man. He is the president of the United States. I am the US senator-elect from the state of Michigan. I am happy to meet with him, like I’ll meet with anyone who can advance the goals I ran on to get money out of politics, put money in pockets, pass Medicare for all,” El-Sayed said.The office of Vice President Vance also confirmed last week that it had started contacting the incoming senator after learning he wanted to meet with the administration.You use AI every day. articles.title: Four years after Amini's death, Iran lashes singer Parastoo Ahmadi 74 times for performing without hijab
articles.summary: Four years after the death of Mahsa Amini in police custody sparked nationwide protests against Iran's compulsory hijab laws, Tehranian singer Parastoo
articles.body: Four years after the death of Mahsa Amini in police custody sparked nationwide protests against Iran's compulsory hijab laws, Tehranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi has been flogged 74 times for performing without a head covering.Ahmadi and four members of her concert team were given 74 lashes each in the city of Qom on Monday, according to defence lawyer Mostafa Nili, cited by Iran Human Rights (IHRNGO). The punishment was carried out at the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom, according to the lawyers.The singer was punished for performing in a sleeveless dress with her hair uncovered during an online concert in December 2024, in "defiance of Iran's mandatory hijab rules."Ahmadi's "Caravanserai Concert" was filmed in December 2024 at the historic Deir-e Gachin Caravanserai near Qom, a city known for its religious seminaries and conservative religious establishment.The performance, which had no live audience, featured Ahmadi singing alongside male musicians. She wore a long black sleeveless dress and performed with her hair uncovered.Iranian authorities subsequently opened a case against Ahmadi and members of her production team over an "illegal concert". The judiciary-affiliated Mizan News Agency said the performance did not comply with the country's "legal and religious standards".A criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others in June of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material". The defendants denied the charges.In addition to the flogging sentence, they were banned from audiovisual activities and leaving the country for two years. An appeals court upheld the ruling in September, according to her lawyers.Four members of her team also floggedThe four men flogged alongside Ahmadi were identified as musicians Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri and Amir-Ali Pirnia, and concert organiser Mohsen Lashkari.A member of the defence team told the BBC that lawyers had tried to get the verdict overturned, reduce the punishment or suspend its execution."We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he said."The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately," he added.The United Nations Human Rights Office condemned the flogging, describing it as "abhorrent" and calling on Iranian authorities to abolish the practice."Flogging is a form of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment, absolutely prohibited under international law in all circumstances. Iran must abstain from carrying out other flogging sentences and eradicate this practice from its laws," it added.Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam, director of IHRNGO told CNN that Ahmadi's clothing was an important factor in the punishment, but the case also involved her decision to sing publicly and her broader challenge to Iranian authorities."A government that is incapable of resolving the crises of livelihoods, water and electricity, yet does not hesitate to flog a woman for her voice, has reached the end of its life," he wrote on X.Iran's compulsory hijab lawsUnder Iranian law, women and girls above the age of puberty are required to cover their hair and wear long, loose-fitting clothing. Public performances by women are also restricted.In September 2022, protests erupted across Iran following the death of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman detained by morality police in Tehran for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly". She died in custody, triggering demonstrations against the country's clerical establishment.Women took to the streets, burning or waving their headscarves, while hundreds were killed in a crackdown by security forces.Since then, many women have stopped covering their hair in public in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with arrests, warnings, business closures and other punitive measures.The pressure on female performers has also continued. Singer Hiva Seyfizadeh was sentenced by a lower court to four years in prison for allegedly "encouraging corruption and prostitution" after performing traditional Iranian music in Tehran in February 2025.In a video posted on social media in August, Seyfizadeh said she had sung only several verses by 13th-century Persian poet Saadi Shirazi and questioned how her performance could amount to encouraging corruption or prostitution.Ahmadi's flogging also reignited accusations of double standards in the Islamic Republic's treatment of female singers, the Iran International reported.In April, as Iran was at war with the United States and Israel, footage of Lebanese singer Julia Boutros was screened at nighttime gatherings of government supporters in Tehran's Ferdows Garden. Boutros is known for her songs in support of the Lebanese resistance.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pune techie lists used mattress online for Rs 15,000, receives QR code from prospective buyer to collect payment, scans it repeatedly after being told transactions failed and loses Rs 3.97 lakh
articles.summary: PUNE: An attempt to sell a used mattress online ended up costing an IT professional nearly Rs 4 lakh.
articles.body: PUNE: An attempt to sell a used mattress online ended up costing an IT professional nearly Rs 4 lakh. The 46-year-old from Phursungi listed the mattress on an online marketplace and was taken in by a fraudster posing as a prospective buyer. He was tricked into scanning QR codes to receive the payment, but each scan resulted in money being debited from his bank account.The fraud took place in Aug and the man lodged a complaint with the Phursungi police on Monday.An officer said on Aug 10, the complainant listed his mattress for Rs 15,000. A man contacted him through the platform and expressed interest in buying it.“The ‘buyer’ took the complainant’s mobile number, said he would make the payment next day and send someone to collect the mattress,” the officer said.According to the complaint, on Aug 11, the suspect sent the complainant a QR code, claiming it was linked to his merchant account and that all he needed to do to receive the payment was to scan it. “He was told that the transaction might initially fail,” the officer said.The man scanned the code using a UPI app and received Rs 2, leading him to believe the process was genuine. “However, when he scanned another code, Rs 15,000 was debited from his account,” the officer said.The fraudster then claimed the payment had failed and persuaded the techie to repeat the process. Believing the earlier transactions would be reversed, he continued scanning QR codes, and losing money.“Seven transactions were carried out on Aug 11, resulting in a total loss of Rs 3.97 lakh. The fraudster subsequently stopped responding to calls and blocked the victim’s number,” the officer said.“We have sought the details of the transactions from his bank,” the officer said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: Bisleri row: FSSAI launches pan-India water quality checks; results within 1-2 months
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water, with the results expected to take at least one to two months, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said.The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts to examine various food categories and ensure compliance with prescribed standards."That process has started, and we're doing it across the country. The results will take at least a month or two," Punhani told reporters.He clarified that packaged drinking water was not selected for any specific reason but was part of the regulator's broader surveillance programme."Last year, we took up dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, sugary drinks and other products. So, water is also part of the process," he added.Separately, Punhani stressed the need for food businesses to follow ethical advertising practices, particularly when making claims about their products and promoting them.He emphasised that the regulator was not looking at the issue solely from a legal perspective and urged industry players to consider the ethical dimensions of advertising."The idea is not that it's only the legal part of it. It is also the ethical part of it," he said, calling on the industry to focus on responsible advertising practices.The Bisleri rowPunhani's remarks and the nationwide surveillance exercise come amid regulatory action against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International over a sample collected from its Goa facility.On November 23, the FSSAI granted sanction to prosecute the company after a regulatory sample was initially found non-compliant with the prescribed limits for bromate and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.Following an appeal by the company, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further examination, which also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).However, the FSSAI clarified on Monday that the action was limited to a single sample from one batch, numbered GO 270, collected from the company's plant at Verna Electronic City in South Goa.Also Read | ‘Only one batch affected’: Bisleri says no stock of Goa-made water under FSSAI scanner in marketThe authority also issued an order prohibiting the sale of the concerned batch under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.Bisleri International subsequently welcomed the clarification, maintaining that the sales prohibition applied only to the specific batch manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.The company stated that it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that no stocks of the particular batch were currently available in the market. It also maintained that retesting found bromate levels below the permissible limit.(With ANI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 40 F-16s, more Mirages: Ukraine's hunt for jets hits wall as Russian drones take toll
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has asked European allies to supply 40 additional F-16 fighters, along with more French-made Mirage 2000 jets, as
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has asked European allies to supply 40 additional F-16 fighters, along with more French-made Mirage 2000 jets, as Russian drones and missiles continue to pound Ukrainian cities. Speaking at the 37th Ukraine Defence Contact Group meeting in Brussels, he said the F-16s already in service spend too much time in repair shops and not enough in the air. Ukraine's fleet comprises early variants of the aircraft, manufactured in the 1980s and early 1990s, whose ageing airframes require more frequent maintenance.Fighters are critical to Ukraine for reasons that extend well beyond aerial combat. Open-source estimates put its F-16 fleet at around 39 aircraft, with the jets reportedly accounting for about 80 per cent of the Air Force's sorties by the end of 2025. They are increasingly being deployed to intercept Russian drones and cruise missiles, a demanding role that puts considerable strain on scarce and expensive airframes. Adding 40 more aircraft would help distribute this operational burden, keep more jets mission-ready and free up capacity for other combat roles.But finding 40 additional F-16s will be no easy task. The United States has ruled out supplying aircraft from its own operational fleet, offering only non-operational airframes for spare parts. Belgium is the only country officially listed as willing to provide more jets, with 10 promised by the end of the year as part of a 30-aircraft commitment made in 2024. Portugal has described a transfer as virtually impossible, while Greece has offered to train Ukrainian pilots but ruled out handing over aircraft. Norway says its remaining airframes are unsuitable for a return to service, and the Netherlands appears to have exhausted its available stock. Denmark has yet to indicate whether it will go beyond its earlier pledge of up to 19 jets. Romania, Turkey, Slovakia, Poland and Bulgaria are also unlikely donors. Analysts caution that upcoming elections in Greece, Slovakia, Poland and France could further complicate transfers, making them politically sensitive.The search for additional Mirage 2000s is equally challenging. France has delivered at least four Mirage 2000-5Fs and pledged two more by the end of 2026, but has little surplus capacity in its inventory. Greece operates 24 upgraded Mirage 2000-5 Mk II fighters, but wants firm commitments on Rafale replacements before considering a transfer. Qatar's 12 retired aircraft are of uncertain serviceability, while the UAE's fleet is tied to its own transition to the Rafale. India, Taiwan and Egypt are considered unlikely suppliers. Zelenskyy has argued that the Mirage can be inducted into Ukrainian service more quickly than the Rafale, which Kyiv plans to acquire in large numbers.

articles.title: 3 dead, 23 trapped after flood hits illegal gold mine in Indonesia
articles.summary: Rescuers recovered three bodies on Wednesday and continued searching for 23 miners believed trapped in a flooded unauthorised gold mine in Indonesia’s
articles.body: Rescuers recovered three bodies on Wednesday and continued searching for 23 miners believed trapped in a flooded unauthorised gold mine in Indonesia’s West Java province. The mines got flooded after heavy rain caused a nearby river to overflow into the shaft.The miners were digging for gold late Monday when the Ciseureuh River flooded the mine in the Pongkor area of Bogor regency, about 60 km south of the capital, Jakarta. The shaft is estimated to be around 100 metres (330 feet) deep.Eleven miners managed to escape from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan told AP. The three victims recovered on Wednesday were found at depths of 30 to 40 metres (100 to 130 feet). Their identities are not immediately known.The rescue operation was complicated by the mine’s narrow entrance, slippery terrain, poor lighting and high water levels. Authorities said the water had not yet receded significantly and draining the shaft could take considerable time.Rescue delayed as illegal operation went unreportedLocal miners and residents initially tried to pump water out of the mine themselves, but the situation soon became unmanageable.Authorities were not immediately informed about the incident because the miners were working at an illegal site, officials said.“The problem was that nobody reported it and nobody wanted to report it because the activity was illegal,” said M Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor disaster mitigation agency, to AP.Police received reports of miners trapped underground about 16 hours after the flooding occurred, Rochmawan said. Local authorities, firefighters and other agencies conducted an initial assessment before state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight on Wednesday, prompting a full-scale rescue operation.Earlier on Wednesday, West Java police said 26 miners had yet to be evacuated. The number fell to 23 after three bodies were recovered.Pumps deployed to drain flooded shaftRescue teams brought in submersible water pumps to remove water from the mine and attempted to seal openings through which groundwater continued to seep in.“We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft,” Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said in a statement.She said the depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting were key considerations in deciding how rescuers could safely proceed.The mine is located near facilities operated by Antam’s Pongkor gold mining unit. The company said the incident occurred at an unauthorised mine and was unrelated to its operations.Antam said all its employees were safe and its operations continued normally. It added that it had repeatedly closed access to illegal mining sites in the area and used patrols, drones and surveillance cameras to deter unauthorised activity.Authorities had closed about 30 gold mine pits in another part of Bogor last week, according to local media reports.Illegal mining remains a major safety riskSmall-scale and unauthorised mining is common in Indonesia, where mineral-rich deposits in remote areas provide livelihoods for thousands of people but are difficult for authorities to regulate.Such operations often take place in dangerous conditions, with miners exposed to flooding, landslides and tunnel collapses. Gold ore processing can also involve highly toxic mercury and cyanide, while workers frequently have little or no protective equipment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 77-year-old Florida man arrested for feeding raccoons; insists the food was meant for 7 stray cats he had cared for over 16 years, which became his family after his son's death in 2010
articles.summary: A 77-year-old man in Jacksonville, Florida, was arrested after wildlife officers accused him of illegally feeding raccoons, but he insists the food was
articles.body: A 77-year-old man in Jacksonville, Florida, was arrested after wildlife officers accused him of illegally feeding raccoons, but he insists the food was meant for seven stray cats he and his wife have cared for over 16 years. Louis Abbruzze, who owns a warehouse on Youngerman Court, says the cats became an important part of their lives after they lost their only son in 2010. He has been leaving the warehouse door slightly open at night so the animals can come inside, eat and shelter from the weather. However, the arrangement eventually attracted the attention of wildlife authorities, who said raccoons were also gathering around the property and consuming the food.Florida man's efforts to care for seven stray cats began in 2010Abbruzze and his wife began looking after stray cats around their warehouse following the death of their only son in 2010. He described caring for the animals as something that helped the couple cope with their loss.Over the years, they trapped the cats, arranged vaccinations and sterilisation, and found homes for several of them. Seven cats remain at the warehouse, where Abbruzze says they continue to receive food and shelter.He described the animals as more than just strays, saying they had become like children to him and his wife. He also credited them with helping the couple find a renewed sense of purpose after their personal tragedy.Dispute with wildlife authorities over raccoonsThe disagreement reportedly began around a year and a half before his arrest, when the property's homeowners association hired new management. According to Abbruzze, the management objected to him leaving the warehouse door open at night and warned that he could face fines or legal action if he continued.Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) officers had also raised concerns about raccoons gathering around the property. Abbruzze said he had previously been warned about leaving food outside and believed he was following the authorities' instructions by feeding the cats and removing the food whenever raccoons appeared.However, the FWC said officers had received complaints about a tenant feeding raccoons and that Abbruzze had previously been cited for providing the animals with food and access to his unit.According to an officer's report cited by USA Today Network, approximately 10 to 15 raccoons were waiting near the back door of the business when the officer arrived.Why was the Florida man arrested?FWC officers arrested Abbruzze on September 15, 2026, on a misdemeanour charge related to feeding wildlife. The arrest followed earlier citations over the same issue.According to Jacksonville Sheriff's Office booking information cited by USA Today Network, he had previously been documented for the same violation three times.Florida law prohibits intentionally feeding certain wildlife, including raccoons, or placing food and rubbish in a manner that attracts them. Under Florida Statutes Section 379.412, repeat violations can result in criminal penalties.The restrictions are intended to prevent wild animals from becoming dependent on human food, losing their natural fear of people or gathering in residential and commercial areas, where they can create safety and property-related problems.Man disputes the allegationsAbbruzze maintains that he never intended to feed raccoons and that his actions were solely aimed at looking after the seven cats. He also described the circumstances of his arrest, saying officers handcuffed him despite his difficulty walking with a broken ankle and a cane.Speaking about the incident, he questioned why he was being treated like a criminal when, according to him, he was simply trying to care for animals.He said he expected to return to court with his attorney the following week.The FWC, meanwhile, maintains that feeding raccoons is prohibited under Florida regulations, regardless of whether other animals are also being fed at the same location.You use AI every day. articles.title: California Wendy’s customer is suing the burger chain and the company behind its checkout software, alleging they worked together to raise menu prices across the US
articles.summary: A longtime Wendy’s customer in California is suing the fast-food chain and NCR Voyix, the company behind its checkout software.
articles.body: A longtime Wendy’s customer in California is suing the fast-food chain and NCR Voyix, the company behind its checkout software. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, the lawsuit alleges that they worked together to raise menu prices across the US. Andy Garcia says Wendy’s used detailed sales data from independently owned restaurants to coordinate prices, leaving customers like him paying more than they would have if the locations had competed on price. He filed the proposed class action 3 in federal court in Maryland.​Garcia says he eats at Wendy’s at least once a week. He is asking to represent people who bought one or more menu items at any US Wendy’s from January 1, 2022, whether the restaurant was run by a franchisee or by Wendy’s itself. The suit seeks monetary damages and a court order to stop the alleged pricing coordination.​How Wendy’s allegedly used data from its checkout software​At the centre of the lawsuit is Aloha, the point-of-sale system supplied by NCR Voyix. The complaint says Wendy’s required franchisees to use the software and provide detailed sales and pricing information, the Reuters report noted. That included data from individual transactions. Garcia alleges that Wendy’s pooled and shared that information across its restaurant network and used it to coordinate menu prices. Reuters​The case turns on who actually decided what customers paid. Restaurants can carry the same Wendy’s name while operating under different owners. Garcia argues that those owners should have been able to compete for customers by setting their own prices. The complaint alleges that Wendy’s instead became a “common decision-maker” for thousands of locations. In Garcia’s account, that arrangement removed an incentive for individual operators to charge less.​Allen Neumark, one of Garcia’s lawyers, said Wendy’s tells investors its franchisees set their own prices. He disputed that account, saying centralised pricing came at customers’ expense. Wendy’s and NCR Voyix did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.Wendy’s previously drew scrutiny when it discussed testing dynamic pricing, which can change prices in response to conditions such as demand. Garcia’s complaint focuses on how prices were set across restaurants and the role their sales data allegedly played in those decisions.​The case follows a separate lawsuit filed against McDonald’s in October over its use of technology to guide menu prices at US franchises. articles.body: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu govt on Wednesday constituted an internal complaints committee (ICC) to inquire into a woman officer’s complaint alleging sexual harassment against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh.The committee will be headed by environment, climate change and forest additional chief secretary Kakarla Usha, welfare of differently abled persons secretary S Madumathi, law secretary P Sumathi and Sunitha Joe are the other members.A govt order cited “representation from a lady officer on Nov 23, 2026,” for setting up the committee.The order said the committee had been constituted to inquire into the complaint against the MLA, who represents the Kallakurichi assembly constituency. “The committee shall make efforts to complete the inquiry within 60 days,” the order said.The govt order was issued by chief secretary M Sai Kumar.The panel has also been directed to take further action, as necessary, under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 on the said complaint.
